skill.name: git-advanced-workflows
skill.description: Plan and verify advanced Git workflows for history cleanup, cherry-picking, bisect debugging, worktrees, and recovery.
skill.summary: Guide advanced Git history, branch, debugging, worktree, and recovery workflows with practical safety checks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. They come from Markdown inline code, fenced Bash examples, and Git worktree paths rather than executable scripts, hidden automation, or prompt-injection content. The skill teaches destructive Git operations, so users should require repository-specific confirmation before changing history.

remediation.issue: Destructive Git examples need explicit safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Add an instruction to confirm branch, remote, backup, and user approval before reset, rebase, or force push commands.
State that parent-directory paths are placeholders and users should choose a safe local destination.

remediation.issue: Command examples could be copied without repository context.
remediation.suggestion: Label command blocks as examples and require status checks before any command changes history.

content.value_statement: Complex Git history changes can damage branches when commands are copied without context. This skill guides rebase, cherry-pick, bisect, worktree, and recovery tasks with checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains interactive rebase operations for cleaning local commit history.
Shows cherry-pick workflows for applying selected commits across branches.
Guides manual and automated bisect sessions to locate regressions.
Describes Git worktrees for parallel branch work without stashing.
Covers reflog-based recovery for deleted commits and mistaken resets.
Compares rebase and merge choices for feature branch updates.
limitations: It does not replace repository-specific review or test execution.
It cannot know team branch policies unless the user provides them.
History rewriting examples can disrupt shared branches if misused.
Remote permissions, hooks, and CI behavior must be verified separately.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Clean Pull Request
use_cases.description: Clean local commits, squash fixups, and verify branch history before review.

use_cases.title: Find a Regression Commit
use_cases.description: Use bisect steps to narrow a bug to the commit that introduced it.

use_cases.title: Recover Lost Git Work
use_cases.description: Use reflog and recovery branches after an accidental reset or branch deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Branch State
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check before advanced Git commands.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current Git situation before I change history. Ask for branch, remote, and collaboration details first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Rebase Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me clean this feature branch with interactive rebase. Include a backup plan, verification steps, and safe push guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a Git bisect session to find when this bug started. Include test selection and reset steps.

prompt_templates.title: Recover After a Bad Reset
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me recover commits after an accidental hard reset. Use reflog reasoning and avoid overwriting current work.

output_examples.input: User asks to clean a feature branch before a pull request.
output: Confirm whether the branch is shared with other collaborators.
Create a backup branch before rewriting local history.
Group commits into logical review units and identify fixup commits.
Run tests and review history before publishing changes.

output_examples.input: User reports that a bug appeared sometime after version 2.1.0.
output: Choose a reliable test that passes on the known good version.
Mark known good and known bad revisions during the bisect process.
Record the first bad commit and reset the bisect session afterward.

output_examples.input: User accidentally reset a branch and wants deleted work back.
output: Inspect reflog entries to identify the previous commit position.
Create a recovery branch before moving the original branch again.
Verify recovered changes before any further history rewrite.

best_practices: Confirm branch ownership and collaboration status before rewriting history.
Create a backup branch before rebase, reset, or recovery operations.
Run tests and inspect history before pushing rewritten commits.
anti_patterns: Force pushing a shared branch without checking for remote updates.
Running destructive reset commands before saving or backing up current work.
Using bisect with a dirty working tree or unreliable test command.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent must decide which commands are safe for the repository.

faq.question: Is interactive rebase safe for shared branches?
faq.answer: Usually no. Rebase rewrites history, so confirm team policy before changing commits others may have used.

faq.question: Can it help recover deleted commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains reflog-based recovery and recovery branches for many recent Git mistakes.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the current branch, target branch, remote status, team sharing status, and the result you want.

faq.question: Does it replace code review or CI?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan Git operations, but tests, review, and CI must still validate the result.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
